title: Ivo and the Verdict
premise: Astrid Eastwick, a retired detective turned failing bookseller, receives two letters on the same morning: one confessing to the twelve-year-old drowning of a girl named Ivo, the other promising that 'the witness is still breathing.' The town of Marrow's Bend has long buried the case, and its most powerful family, the Verdicts, built their fortune on the official ruling of accident. As Astrid follows a trail of misfiled evidence and coerced testimony, he discovers the supposed-dead witness is alive, hidden by someone inside the police force itself. The climax forces Astrid to choose between handing the truth to a corrupt court or delivering his own verdict outside the law; in the end, justice arrives not through arrest but through exposure — the confession letter was written by Ivo's sister, who has spent twelve years waiting for Astrid to be brave enough to read it aloud.
about_author: Wren Ravensworth is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade watching cases close too neatly. They write mysteries about the paperwork that buries the truth and the people who refuse to sign off on it.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. On the same grey Tuesday, Astrid opens two unsigned letters among his shop's mail: one confessing to Ivo Verdict's drowning twelve years ago, the other stating only 'the witness is still breathing.' The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine — Astrid recognizes the handwriting on both envelopes as the same.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Lies
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Searching his old case files stored above the bookshop, Astrid finds pages deliberately misfiled under wrong names — including Ivo's autopsy report with a missing toxicology page. The beat is quiet fury: someone he once trusted curated these files for him to find, or never to find.

chapters.title: What the Verdict Family Owns
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Astrid and young constable Nell Brandt. Astrid visits the Verdict estate under the pretense of selling rare books; patriarch Edmund Verdict is charming and chillingly aware of why he's come. Nell, meanwhile, is ordered by her superiors to drop an anonymous records request. Beat: power flexing politely.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. He tracks down Maren Cole, the coroner's assistant from twelve years ago, now living under another name. She admits she was pressured to falsify the timeline but swears she never signed the final report — because there was no final report until weeks later. Beat: guilt finally given a voice.

chapters.title: Dead Men File Taxes
chapters.summary: POV: Nell. Following a paper trail, Nell discovers the 'dead' witness, Tomas Reeve, has been paying taxes under an alias for a decade — meaning someone in the system protected him. Her discovery gets her suspended within hours. Beat: the cost of looking closer.

chapters.title: Fire in the Fiction Section
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The bookshop burns at night; Astrid escapes with only the misfiled files, saved by instinct. Among the ashes investigators find accelerant and a button from a Verdict estate uniform. Beat: escalation — the corruption has stopped being patient.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Chose to Vanish
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid finds Tomas Reeve alive in a coastal caravan park. Reeve saw what happened to Ivo — that Edmund's son killed him in panic, and Edmund arranged everything after — but reveals he stayed silent because they threatened someone he loved. Beat: cowardice understood, not forgiven.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Waiting
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The confession letter's author is revealed: Ivo's sister, Lena, who sent it to force Astrid out of retirement, believing only he had the nerve to finish what he abandoned years ago. Her anger at him mirrors his own shame. Beat: the detective becomes the accused.

chapters.title: The Verdict Delivered
chapters.summary: POV: multiple, converging. At the town's anniversary gala, Astrid publicly reads the confession, the missing toxicology page, and Reeve's sworn statement before the crowd and a recording Nell smuggled in. Edmund's son breaks; Edmund does not. Beat: cathartic climax — truth spoken where power cannot silence it.

chapters.title: Shelved Under Justice
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Trials begin; the old guard falls; Nell is reinstated. Astrid reopens the bookshop, alphabetizing a new section: true accounts of Marrow's Bend, starting with Ivo's name spelled correctly. Final beat: bittersweet peace — justice came late, outside the law, and it cost everyone something.
